opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kathryn Bishop (employee ID E023) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E023.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kathryn Bishop (E023), Engineer, full-time employee. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write access; write does not require system ownership. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows E023 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read access, never admin, and write requires advanced training. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The security record for E023 indicates she is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors with basic training max out at read access (write requires advanced security training; admin is never allowed for contractors). The requested write level exceeds the maximum of read, so the maximum, read, is granted.

Actually, let me reconsider. The notes are both about the same ticket 1. The team memory shows 2 notes. One note says full_time, other says contractor.
